notes: Two English 'the's against one article morpheme. Rule 29's fronting clause governs only a chain whose rectum is rendered anarthrously; here the ASV writes 'the Levites', so the article keeps its own 'the' and the construct מִשְׁפְּחוֹת takes a supplied one. The parallel in v.33 is resolved the same way.

'fathers houses' is kept whole under rule 31 with the head on 'fathers'. A competing reading would mark the italic 'houses' 'added', since 'according to their fathers' would already render לַאֲבוֹתֵיהֶם; the unit as written is defensible, but that alternative is worth recording.
לְ correctly takes the multi-word 'according to' headed on 'according' rather than the connective (rule 24).
